1.title: Connect the white and blue wires
1.say: Hold the small white board steady on the table. Push the white thin wire into a top hole on the left side. Push the blue thin wire into a top hole on the right side.
placements: white thin insulated wire from battery minus side → top edge 5-hole cross row on left side of small white plug board, pushed about one centimetre deep by fingers until firm, sharing row with future resistor leg; in the video: left top hole area

blue thin insulated wire from battery plus side → top edge 5-hole cross row on right side of same board, several holes to the right of white wire in a different connected group, pushed about one centimetre deep by fingers until firm, sharing row with future LED long leg; in the video: right top hole area
watch_for: if both wires sit in the same connected 5-hole row the power is shorted, lift one wire to a different group a few holes away
if a wire feels loose or falls out it is not deep enough, push it straight down about one centimetre until it grips
1.check_yourself: It should look like the small white board sitting flat with a white wire sticking up on the left top and a blue wire sticking up on the right top.

2.title: Add the striped resistor across
2.say: Push one leg of the blue striped resistor into the row with the white wire. Push the other leg into a free row a few holes to the right.
placements: small blue striped resistor with two thin wire legs → across top of board with left leg in same 5-hole cross row as white wire on left side and right leg in a separate 5-hole cross row a few holes to the right toward the middle, body lying flat just above board, legs pushed by fingers; in the video: body across top left to middle
watch_for: if both legs of the striped resistor share the same 5-hole row the resistor is bypassed, move one leg to a different row a few holes away
if a leg sits in the same row as the blue wire instead of the white wire the circuit stays open, move the left leg to share the white wire row
2.check_yourself: It should look like a tiny blue striped tube lying flat across the top of the board with thin legs going down on the left and middle.

3.title: Plug in the blue LED
3.say: Hold the small blue dome light with two thin legs between your fingers. Push the short leg into the row that holds the resistor end. Push the long leg into the row that holds the blue wire.
placements: blue domed LED light with one long plus leg and one short minus leg with flat side → upright on right side of board with short leg in same 5-hole cross row as right leg of resistor and long leg in same 5-hole cross row as blue wire a hole or two away, pushed by fingers until seated with dome above board; in the video: right edge top area glowing blue
watch_for: if the light stays dark the legs are probably swapped, pull it out and swap so the long leg shares the blue wire row and the short leg shares the resistor row
if the light glows only when you hold it its legs are loose, push each leg straight down until seated
3.check_yourself: It should look like the small blue dome standing straight up on the right side of the board and glowing bright blue.
